questions.q: The coefficient of ${x}^{2012}$ in the expansion of ${\left(1 - x\right)}^{2008}{\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)}^{2007}$ is equal to _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $y = {\left(1 - x\right)}^{2008}{\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)}^{2007}$

$⇒ y = \left(1 - x\right){\left(1 - x\right)}^{2007}{\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)}^{2007}$

$⇒ y = \left(1 - x\right){\left[\left(1 - x\right)\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)\right]}^{2007}$

$⇒ y = \left(1 - x\right){\left(1 - {x}^{3}\right)}^{2007}$

$⇒ y = \left(1 - x\right)\left(C0 2007 - C1 2007 \left({x}^{3}\right) + . . . . . .\right)$

General term in the expansion is given by,

${T}_{r + 1} = \left(1 - x\right)\left(Cr 2007 {x}^{3r}{\left(- 1\right)}^{r}\right)$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1}{=}^{2007}{C}_{r}{x}^{3r}{\left(- 1\right)}^{r} - {}^{2007}{C}_{r}{x}^{3r + 1}{\left(- 1\right)}^{r}$

For coefficient of ${x}^{12}$,

$3r = 2012$

But, $r \ne \dfrac{2012}{3}$

Also, $3r + 1 = 2012$

$⇒ 3r = 2011$

But, $r \ne \dfrac{2011}{3}$

Hence, there is no term containing ${x}^{2012}$.

So coefficient of ${x}^{2012} = 0$

questions.q: The ratio of the coefficient of the middle term in the expansion of $( 1 + x{)}^{20}$ and the sum of the coefficients of two middle terms in expansion of $( 1 + x{)}^{19}$& is& & & & & .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
In& \left(1 + x\right)n$, if~$n$~is even, then the middle term is~\left(\dfrac{n}{2} + 1\right)th$~term.

So, Coefficient~of middle term in $( 1 + x{)}^{20} = C10 20$

In~\left(1 + x\right)n$, if~$n$~is odd, then the middle term is~\left(\dfrac{n + 1}{2}\right)th \text{ and } \left(\dfrac{n + 3}{2}\right)th$~term.

So, Sum of Coefficient~of two middle terms in

$( 1 + x{)}^{19} = C9 19 + C10 19$

So required ratio $= \dfrac{C10 20}{C9 19 + C10 19} = \dfrac{C10 20}{C10 20} = 1$

questions.q: Let the sixth term in the binomial expansion of& \left(\sqrt{{2}^{\log_{2}\left(10 - {3}^{x}\right)}} + {2}^{( x - 2 ) \log_{2}3}5\right)m$ powers of ${2}^{\left(x - 2\right)\log_{2}3}$, be $21$ . If the binomial coefficients of the second, third and fourth terms in the expansion are respectively the first, third and fifth terms of an A.P., then the sum of the squares of all possible values of $x$ is _____ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Binomial expression,

\left(\sqrt{{2}^{\log_{2}\left(10 - {3}^{x}\right)}} + {2}^{( x - 2 ) \log_{2}3}5\right)m$

\left(\sqrt{ \left($10 - {3}^{x}\right)} + {3}^{( x - 2 )}5\right)m$

Now,~${T}_{6} = C5 m \left(10 - {3}^{x}\right)\dfrac{m - 5}{2} \cdot\left({3}^{x - 2}\right) =$21 \ldots \left($1\right)$

Also given,

$C1 m , C2 m , C3 m$~are in A.P.

So,~$2 $\cdot$C2 m = C1 m + C3 m$

$⇒ 2 $\times \dfrac{m !}{2 ! \left(m - 2\right) !} =$m + $\dfrac{m !}{3 ! \left(m - 3\right) !}

Solving for $m$, we get $m = 2, 7$~and~$m = 2$~(rejected), so $m = 7$

Put in equation \left(1\right)$

$21 \cdot \left($10 - {3}^{x}\right)$\dfrac{3x}{9} =$21$

$⇒ \left($10 - {3}^{x}\right){3}^{x} = 9 $\times$1$

$⇒ {3}^{x} = {3}^{0}, {3}^{2}$

$⇒ x = 0, 2$

Sum of the squares of all possible values of $x = 4.

$

questions.q: The number of rational terms in the binomial expansion of \left(4\dfrac{1}{4} + 5\dfrac{1}{6}\right)120$is_______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

\left(4\dfrac{1}{4} + 5\dfrac{1}{6}\right)120$

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 120 \left(4\dfrac{1}{4}\right)120 - r\left(5\right)\dfrac{r}{6}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 120 \left(2\right)\dfrac{120 - r}{2}\left(5\right)\dfrac{r}{6}$
~

For rational terms $r = 6\lambda, 0 \le r \le 120$, hence

$r = 0, 6, 12, . . . , 120$

So, total number of rational terms are $21$.

$

questions.q: If the coefficient of $x^{10}$~in the binomial expansion of \left(\dfrac{x}{5\dfrac{1}{4}} + \dfrac{5}{x\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)60$~is ${5}^{k}l$, where $l, k \in N$~and $l$~is coprime to $5$, then $k$ \text{ and } is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 60 \left(\dfrac{x}{5\dfrac{1}{4}}\right)60 - r\left(\dfrac{5}{x\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)r$

For~$x^{10}$,~$\dfrac{60 - r}{2} - \dfrac{r}{3} = 10 ⇒ r = 24$

Hence coefficient of $x^{10}$ will be $C24 60 {5}^{3}$

Now, exponent of $5$ in $C24 60$~will be the power of~$5$~in~$\dfrac{60 !}{24 ! 36 !}\text{i.e.}\dfrac{514}{{5}^{4} \cdot {5}^{8}} = {5}^{2}$

i.e.~$k = 5$

questions.q: If \left(\dfrac{36}{44}\right)k$ is the term, independent of $x,$~in the binomial expansion of \left(\dfrac{x}{4} - \dfrac{12}{x2}\right)12,$~then $k$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that& \left(\dfrac{x}{4} - \dfrac{12}{x2}\right)12$

$r^{th}$~term of an expression is~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n x^{n - r}y^{r}$~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 12 \left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right)12 - r\left(- \dfrac{12}{x2}\right)r = Cr 12 \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)12 - r ( - 12{)}^{r} \cdot x^{12 - r - 2r}$
$⇒ 12 - 3r = 0$
$⇒ r = 4$

So term independent from $x$ is ${T}_{5} = C4 12 \cdot \dfrac{1}{48} \cdot {3}^{4} \cdot {4}^{4} = C4 12 \cdot \dfrac{34}{44}$

We know that~$Cr n = \dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r\right) ! r !}$

$= 55 \times \dfrac{36}{44}$

They given that it is~$= k\dfrac{36}{44}$

So required value of~$k = 55 .$

$

questions.q: Let the coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of $( 1 + 2x{)}^{n}$ be in the ratio $2: 5: 8$. Then the coefficient of the term, which is in the middle of these three terms, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of $( 1 + 2x{)}^{n}$ be in the ratio $2: 5: 8$.

Now~$r^{th}$~term in expansion of~$( 1 + 2x{)}^{n}$~is given by,~${t}_{r + 1} = Cr n ( 2x{)}^{r}$

Now let~${T}_{r}, {T}_{r + 1}, {T}_{r + 2}$~are in the ratio~$2: 5: 8$

$⇒ \dfrac{Tr}{Tr + 1} = \dfrac{Cr - 1 n ( 2{)}^{r - 1}}{Cr n ( 2{)}^{r}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{n !( r - 1 ) ! ( n - r + 1 ) !}{n ! ( 2 )r ! ( n - r ) !} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{r}{n - r + 1} = \dfrac{4}{5} ⇒ 5r = 4n - 4r + 4$~

$⇒ 9r = 4 ( n + 1 ) . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now taking other ratio~\dfrac{Tr + 1}{Tr + 2} = \dfrac{Cr n ( 2{)}^{r}}{Cr + 1 n ( 2{)}^{r + 1}} = \dfrac{5}{8}

$⇒ $\dfrac{n !r ! ( n - r ) !}{n !( r + 1 ) ! ( n - r - 1 ) !} = \dfrac{5}{4}$⇒ $\dfrac{r + 1}{n - r} = \dfrac{5}{4}

$⇒ 4r + 4 = 5n - 5r$

$⇒ 5n - 4 = 9r . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation~ \left($1\right) & \left(2\right)$~we get,

$4n + 4 = 5n - 4 ⇒ n = 8$~and~$r = 4$

So, coefficient of middle term will be

$C4 8 {2}^{4} = 16 \times \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 5}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} =16 \times70 = 1120

$

questions.q: If the coefficients of $x$ and $x^{2}$~in the expansion of \left(1 + x\right)p\left(1 - x\right)q, p, q \le 15$, are $- 3$~and~$- 5$ respectively, then the coefficient of $x^{3}$ \text{ and } is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given& coefficient of& $x$~in expansion of \left(1 + x\right)p \left(1 - x\right)q$~is~$- 3$

$⇒ C0 q C1 p - C0 p C1 q = - 3$

$⇒ p - q = - 3 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now coefficients of~$x^{2}$~in expansion of~\left(1 + x\$right)p\left($1 - x\right)q$

$- C1q P {C}_{1} + C0 q C2 P + C0 P C2 q = - 5$

$⇒ - pq + \dfrac{p \left($p - 1\right)}${2} + $\dfrac{q \left(q - 1\right)}${2} = -$5 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Solving~ \left(1\right)$~and~ \left(2\right)$

$p = 8, q = 11$

Coefficient of~$x^{3}$~in expansion of \left(1 + x\right)p\left(1 - x\right)q$~will be,

$- C3 q + C3 p + {C p}_{1}^{q}{C}_{2} - {C p}_{2}^{q}{C}_{1}$

$= - C3 11 + C3 8 + C1 8 C2 11 - C2 8 C1 11$

$= 23$

$

questions.q: If the constant term, in binomial expansion of \left(2x^{r} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)10$ is $180,$ then $r$ is equal to ____________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The general term in the binomial expansion of& \left(a + b\right)n$~is~$CR n a^{n - R}b^{R} .$

Thus, the general term in the expansion of~\left(2x^{r} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)10$~is~$= CR 10 \left(2x^{r}\right)10 - R\left(\dfrac{1}{x2}\right)R$

$= CR 10 \left({2}^{10 - R}x^{r\left(10 - R\right)}\right)x^{- 2R}$

Given, the constant term in the expansion is~$180$

$⇒ CR 10 \cdot {2}^{10 - R} = 180 \ldots \left(1\right)$~

And~$( 10 - R ) r - 2R = 0$

$⇒ r = $\dfrac{2R}{10 - R}

$⇒ r = $\dfrac{2 ( R - 10 )}{10 - R} + \dfrac{20}{10 - R}

$⇒ r = - 2 + $\dfrac{20}{10 - R} \ldots \left(2\right)$

Since~$R$~is positive~integer less than or equal to~$10$~and~$r$~is also an integer,~hence, the value of~$R$~is such that, $10 - R$~must divide~$20 .$

This is possible, when the value of~$10 - R$~can be one from the divisors of~$20$~i.e.~$10 - R$~can be from~$1, 2, 4$~or~$5$~and consequently,~$R$~can be~$9, 8, 6$~or~$5$~respectively.

But for~$R = 9, 6 & 5$~equation \left(1\right)$~is~ not satisfied, hence~$R = 8$

as~$CR 10 {2}^{10 - R} = 180$

$⇒ r = $\dfrac{2 \times 8}{10 - 8} =$8 .

$

questions.q: Let the coefficients of third, fourth and fifth terms in the expansion of \left(x + \dfrac{a}{x2}\right)n, x \ne 0,$ be in the ratio $12: 8: 3 .$~Then the term independent of $x$ in the expansion, is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The general term in the expansion of& \left(a + b\right)n$~is~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n a^{n - r}b^{r} .$

Hence, the general term in the expansion of~\left(x + \dfrac{a}{x2}\right)n$~is~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n ( x{)}^{n - r}\left(\dfrac{a}{x2}\right)r$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr n a^{r}x^{n - 3r}$

Given the coefficients of third, fourth and fifth terms are in the ratio~$12: 8: 3$

$⇒ \left(C2 n a^{2}\right): \left(C3 n a^{3}\right): C4 n a^{4} = 12: 8: 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{C2 n a^{2}}{C3 n a^{3}} = \dfrac{12}{8}$~and~$\dfrac{C3 n a^{3}}{C4 n a^{4}} = \dfrac{8}{3}$

Using~$\dfrac{Cr n}{Cr + 1 n} = \dfrac{r + 1}{n - r},$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{\left(n - 2\right)a} = \dfrac{3}{2}$~and~$\dfrac{4}{\left(n - 3\right)a} = \dfrac{8}{3}$

On dividing the two equations, we get~$\dfrac{3\left(n - 3\right)}{4\left(n - 2\right)} = \dfrac{9}{16}$

$⇒ 4n - 12 = 3n - 6$

$⇒ n = 6$~and~$a = \dfrac{1}{2} .$

For term independent of $x ⇒ n = 3r$

$⇒ r = 2 .$

$∴$~The coefficient is$C2 6 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 = \dfrac{15}{4} .$

Hence, the nearest integer is $4 .$

questions.q: In the expansion of \left(1 + x\right)\left(1 - x^{2}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{3}{x2} + \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)5, x \ne 0$, the sum of the coefficient of $x^{3}$ and $x^{- 13} is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(1 + x\right)\left(1 - x^{2}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{3}{x2} + \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)5$

$= \left(1 + x\right)2\left(1 - x\right)\left(\dfrac{x^{3} + 3x^{2} + 3x + 1}{x3}\right)5$

$= \left(1 + x\right)2\left(1 - x\right)\left(\dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)3}{x3}\right)5$

$= \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)17\left(1 - x\right)}{x15}$

$= \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)17}{x15} - \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)17}{x14}$

Now for coefficient of $x^{3}$, we will find coefficient of $x^{18}$ in expansion of \left(1 + x\right)17$ which is not possible and $x^{17}$ in expansion of $- \left(1 + x\right)17$ which will be $- C17 17 = - 1$

And for coefficient of $x^{- 13}$ we will coefficient of $x^{2}$ in expansion of \left(1 + x\right)17$ which will be $C2 17$ and coefficient of $x$ in expansion of $- \left(1 + x\right)17$ which will be $- C1 17$, so the coefficient of $x^{- 13}$ will be $C2 17 - C1 17 = 136 - 17 = 119$

Hence, the sum will be $119 - 1 = 118$

$

questions.q: Let&  \left[t\right]$~denote the greatest integer~$\le t$. if the~constant term in the expansion of~  \left(3x^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2x^{5}}\right)7$~is~$\alpha$~then~\left[\alpha\right]~is equal to~_____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given expansion is& \left(3x^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2x^{5}}\right)7$.

The~general term in the binomial expansion of~\left(x + a\right)n$~is given by~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n x^{n - r}a^{r}$.

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 7 \left(3x^{2}\right)7 - r\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2x^{5}}\right)r$

$= Cr 7 \left(- 1\right)r\left(\dfrac{37 - r}{2r}\right)x^{14 - 2r - 5r}$

Now for term independent of~$x⇒ 14 - 2r - 5r = 0$

$⇒ r = 2$

Coefficient of~$x^{0}$~is~$C2 7 \left(-1\right)2 \times\left(\dfrac{37 - 2}{22}\right)

$= $\dfrac{7 \times 6}{2} \times \dfrac{35}{22}.

$⇒ $\alpha = \dfrac{5103}{4}

$⇒ \left[\alpha\right] =$1275$

Hence& this is the required answer.

questions.q: If the coefficient of $x^{30}$ in the expansion of \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)6\left(1 + x^{2}\right)7\left(1 - x^{3}\right)8; x \ne 0$ is $\alpha$, then \left|\alpha\right|$ equals _________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given expansion is \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)6\left(1 + x^{2}\right)7\left(1 - x^{3}\right)8$.

Now, coefficient of $x^{30}$ in $\dfrac{\left(x + 1\right)6\left(1 + x^{2}\right)7\left(1 - x^{3}\right)8}{x6}$

So, we will find the coefficient of $x^{36}$ in \left(1 + x\right)6\left(1 + x^{2}\right)7\left(1 - x^{3}\right)8$

General term of the given expansion is${}^{6}{C{r}_{1}}^{7}{C{r}_{2}}^{8}{C}_{r3}\left(- 1\right){r}_{3}x^{{r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} + 3{r}_{3}}$.

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} + 3{r}_{3} = 36$

Case-I:

${r}_{1}$ ${r}_{2}$ ${r}_{3}$
$0$ $6$ $8$
$2$ $5$ $8$
$4$ $4$ $8$
$6$ $3$ $8$

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} = 12$ (Taking ${r}_{3} = 8$)

Case II:

${r}_{1}$ ${r}_{2}$ ${r}_{3}$
$1$ $7$ $7$
$3$ $6$ $7$
$5$ $5$ $7$

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} = 15$ (Taking ${r}_{3} = 7$)

Case III:

${r}_{1}$ ${r}_{2}$ ${r}_{3}$
$4$ $7$ $6$
$6$ $6$ $6$

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} = 18$ (Taking ${r}_{3} = 6$)

So, the required coefficient Is given by, $\alpha = 7 + \left(15 \times 21\right) + \left(15 \times 35\right) + \left(35\right) - \left(6 \times 8\right) - \left(20 \times 7 \times 8\right) - \left(6 \times21 \times8\right) + \left($15 \times28\right) + \left($7 \times28\right)$

$⇒ $\alpha = -$678$

$⇒ \left|\alpha\right| =$678$

$

questions.q: Let& $\alpha$~be the constant term in the binomial expansion of~\left(\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{6}{x\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)n, n \le 15 .$~If the sum of the coefficients of the remaining terms in the expansion is $649$ and the coefficient of $x^{- n}$~is~$\lambda\alpha,$ then~$\lambda$ is equal to~________ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{6}{x\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)n, n \le 15$

Now $r^{th}$~term is given by

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n \left(x\dfrac{1}{2}\right)n - r\left(- 6x\dfrac{- 3}{2}\right)r$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = \left(- 6\right)r \cdot Cr n \cdot x\dfrac{n - r}{2} \cdot x\dfrac{- 3r}{2}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = \left(- 6\right)r \cdot Cr n \cdot x\dfrac{n - 4r}{2}$

Now we have to take,~$n = 4r$~for constant term so~$n$~is divisible by~$4 .$

So,~$\alpha = C\dfrac{n}{4} n \left(- 6\right)\dfrac{n}{4}$

And sum of all coefficients~will be~\left(\sqrt{1} - \dfrac{6}{1\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)n = \left(- 5\right)n$

Also given,~\left(- 5\right)n - C\dfrac{n}{4} n \left(- 6\right)\dfrac{n}{4} = 649$

Now by hit and trial we get,~$n = 4$

Hence,~$\alpha = C1 4 \left(- 6\right)\dfrac{4}{4} = - 24$

Now for coefficient of~$x^{- 4}$

$\dfrac{n - 4r}{2} = - 4$

$⇒ n = 4r - 8 ⇒ r = 3$

So,~$\lambda\left(\alpha\right) = \left(- 6\right)3 \cdot C3 4$

$⇒ \lambda\left(- 24\right) = \left(- 6\right)3 \cdot C3 4$

$⇒ \lambda = 36$

$

$\begin{aligned} & \text { By } \frac{(i)}{(\text { ii) }} \\ & \frac{{ }^n C_1}{{ }^n C_2} \frac{x}{y}=\frac{9}{2}...(iv) \\ & \text { By } \frac{(\text { ii) }}{(\text { iii) }} \\ & \frac{{ }^n C_2}{{ }^n C_3} \frac{x}{y}=9....(v)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { By } \frac{(\text { iv })}{(v)} \\ & \frac{{ }^n C_1{ }^n C_3}{{ }^n C_2{ }^n C_2}=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \frac{2 n^2(n-1)(n-2)}{6}=\frac{n(n-1)}{2} \frac{n(n-1)}{2} \\ & 4 n-8=3 n-3 \\ & \Rightarrow n=5 \\ & \text { put in (v) }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \frac{x}{y}=9 \\ & x=9 y \\ & \text { put in (i) } \\ & { }^5 C_1 x^4\left(\frac{x}{9}\right)=135 \\ & x^5=27 \times 9 \\ & \Rightarrow x=3, \quad y=\frac{1}{3} \\ & 6\left(n^3+x^2+y\right) \\ & =6\left(125+9+\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ & =806\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The term independent of $x$~in the expansion of~\left[\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2 / 3} - x^{1 / 3} + 1} - \dfrac{x - 1}{x - x^{1 / 2}}\right]10, x \ne 1$, is equal to ___.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& \left[\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2 / 3} - x^{1 / 3} + 1} - \dfrac{x - 1}{x - x^{1 / 2}}\right]10$

$⇒ \left(\left(x^{1 / 3} + 1\right) - \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x} + 1}{x}\right)\right)10$

$⇒ \left(x^{1 / 3} - x^{- 1 / 2}\right)10$

General term is~${T}_{r + 1} = 10{C}_{r}\left(x^{1 / 3}\right)10 - r\left(- x^{- 1 / 2}\right)r$

$∴ \dfrac{10 - r}{3} - \dfrac{r}{2} = 0 ⇒ 20 - 2r - 3r = 0$

$⇒ r = 4$

Then,~${T}_{5} = C4 10 = \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 210$

$

Given,

The coefficient of $x^{9}$~in \left(\alphax^{3} + \dfrac{1}{\betax}\right)11$and the~coefficient of $x^{- 9}$ in \left(\alphax - \dfrac{1}{\betax^{3}}\right)11$ are equal,

Now the~$r^{th}$~term of~\left(\alphax^{3} + \dfrac{1}{\betax}\right)11$~is given by~$= Cr 11 \cdot \dfrac{\alpha11 - r}{\betar} \times x^{3\left(11 - r\right) - r}$

So, for~$x^{9}$,~$33 - 4r = 9 ⇒ r = 6$

Hence, coefficient of $x^{9}$~in \left(\alphax^{3} + \dfrac{1}{\betax}\right)11 = C6 11 \cdot \dfrac{\alpha5}{\beta6}$

Similarly, for coefficient of~$x^{- 9}$~in~\left(\alphax - \dfrac{1}{\betax^{3}}\right)11 = - C5 11 \cdot \dfrac{\alpha6}{\beta5}$

Now given both coefficient~are equal,

So,~$\dfrac{11}{C6} \cdot \dfrac{\alpha5}{\beta6} = - \dfrac{11}{C5} \cdot \dfrac{\alpha6}{\beta5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{β} = - \alpha$

$⇒ \alpha\beta = - 1$

$⇒ ( \alpha\beta{)}^{2} = 1$

$

questions.q: The coefficient of& $x^{18}$~in the expansion of~\left(x^{4} - \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)15~is~____________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Binomial expression& \left(x^{4} - \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)15$

Now general term is given by,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 15 \left(x^{4}\right)15 - r\left(- \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)r$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 15 x^{60 - 7r} ( - 1{)}^{r}$

For coefficient of~$x^{18},$~equate~$60 - 7r = 18$

$⇒ r = 6$

Coefficient of~$x^{18} = \left(- 1\right)6 \cdot C6 15 = 5005$

$

questions.q: Let he sum of the coefficient of first three terms in the expansion of& \left(x - \dfrac{3}{x2}\right)n; x = 0, n \in N$~be~$376$. Then, the coefficient of~$x^{4}$ \text{ and } is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that general term in the expansion of& \left(x - \dfrac{3}{x2}\right)n$~is given by,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n x^{n - r}\left(\dfrac{- 3}{x2}\right)r$

$= \left(- 1\right)r \times Cr n {3}^{r}x^{n - r - 2r}$

${T}_{r + 1} = \left(-1\right)r \timesCr n {3}^{r}x^{n - 3r} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

So,~${T}_{1} = {T}_{0 + 1} = C0 n {3}^{0}x^{n} = x^{n}$

${T}_{2} = \left(-1\right) \timesC1 n {3}^{1}x^{n - 3}$

${T}_{3} = C2 n {3}^{2}x^{n - 6}$

Now given sum is

$1 - C1 n \cdot3 + C2 n \cdot {3}^{2} =376$

$⇒ 1 - 3n + $\dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)}{2} \cdot$9 = 376$

$⇒ 1 - 3n + $\dfrac{n^{2} - n}{2} \cdot$9 = 376$

$⇒ 2 - 6n + 9n^{2} - 9n = 752$

$⇒ 9n^{2} - 15n - 750 = 0$

$⇒ 3n^{2} - 5n - 250 = 0$

$⇒ n = $\dfrac{5 \pm \sqrt{25 + 3000}}{6}

$⇒ n = $\dfrac{5 \pm 55}{6}

$⇒ n = $10 \left$\{\text{ignoring negative sign}\right$\}

Now,~${T}_{r + 1} = \left(-$1\right)r Cr 10 {3}^{r}x^{10 - 3r}$

So, for coefficient of $x^{4}$~we take~

$10 - 3r = 4$

$⇒ 3r = 6$

$⇒ r = 2$

So, coefficient of~$x^{4}$~is given by,

${T}_{2 + 1} = \left(-$1\right)2 \cdotC2 10 {3}^{2} = 45 \times9 = 405$.

$
